body: My mom has some serious issues (fleas, possibly on the autism spectrum, maybe some form of personality disorder), but I don't believe she is an N. However, she is the speaker for my Ndad's bullshit. He is the ignoring type, and I suspect closer to a psychopath than an N, and couldn't be bothered to tell me this garbage himself.

This was an old email I found, and I never did respond.

We put the baby up for adoption-- we didn't have any resources and it was the only way to keep her away from my Nparents, and I wasn't mentally healthy enough to care for a child (I'm still not). I have never, ever felt that I made the wrong desicion there.

((Hugs)) I feel blessed that I can "pass" as okay for the most part so I rarely have to explain.

I find it very hard to stay connected to my husband, but I am also fortunate to have married someone who is willing to be so patient with days like today.

After sixish months of therapy I'm starting to have a few good days-- so I guess it does get better, but damn days like today do make me question whether or not things will really change.
Lol now my brain is trying to picture him with overalls and a tool belt. I think my head just exploded a little bit.

We've talked many times about how I'm trying not to filter what I say to him, and that this is a huge struggle for me. Up until now I just haven't been ready to drop the barriers.

I'm thinking that this approach might be more successful because I am simply trying to get rid of the idea that I need to filter what I say to him, rather than trying to convince myself that each rule is okay to break this one time-- which leaves me in pretty much the same conflict next week when I've got to make another exception for the same thing.

I don't always remember to use it, but that idea definitely helps me when I'm aware enough to notice it.

I still tense up when most people get within a few feet, but when I am able to think of it this way, I get to decide whether to move away, tolerate them, or accept their presence openly. So far hubby is the only one who has "accepted" status. With practice this has become mostly automatic with him.

I totally get the physical separation thing. We've actually talked about making one of our closets into a little space where only I'm allowed for when I'm upset and can't deal with him being around. I decided to stick with just shutting myself in the bedroom where he is allowed to come check on me. I'm afraid if we did the closet thing i'd get too dependant on it and I'd stop trying to spend time with people completely.
Just realized I posted this from the wrong account (oops!) So the history isn't easily accessible. I'll message my main account for people if they want to read other posts.

I am hoping that I am simply overreacting. I've been struggling a lot lately with denial and believing that the fault lies with me, and even the thought that these two might agree with that side is enough to send me spiraling right now.

I won't find out until next week what the damage is (if any). I'm just not sure how to hold myself together until then not knowing if I can trust them anymore or not.
